title: Put a gas cooktop's knobs back on: find each D stem by feel with light pressure, push home at OFF, never turn the gas on
instruction: Put the two burner knobs back on their valve stems, each pushed fully home with its pointer at OFF, and leave every burner off.
context: Most US homes cook on a range, about 38% with gas (EIA RECS 2020), and pulling the knobs off to clean round them, then putting them back, is a routine chore. A knob goes on only with the flat in its bore lined up with the flat on the stem, which the knob hides, so you rest it on the stem and turn it until it drops on. Gas valves are push-to-turn: the stem is locked at OFF until it is pushed in. Pressed lightly, the lock holds the stem while the knob turns, and stops the knob once it has dropped on; pressed hard while turning, the stem goes in and turns with the knob, and the gas is on. The skill is a force-limited search by feel, then a straight push home without twisting. Refitting a burner head or a microwave turntable is also 'turn until it drops in', but pushing harder is harmless there; LIBERO's and RoboCasa's stove tasks turn a knob that is already on.
setup: Station table, one fixed layout (x forward from the arms, y to the left, heights above the table top). A gas cooktop section, 270 mm front to back by 400 mm across (x 0.20 to 0.47 m, centred on y 0): a 1 mm black-enamelled steel top panel 42 mm above the table on a 40 mm plywood valve box with a clear acrylic front. At the back, two sealed burners (90 mm bases, 70 mm caps) at x 0.385, y +-0.10 m; grates off. Along the front, two unplumbed push-to-turn surface-burner valves (for example Whirlpool WPW10206288; no gas connected) screwed under the panel, their stems up through 12 mm holes at x 0.265, y +-0.050 m (100 mm apart). Each stem: a 1/4 in (6.35 mm) brass D shaft, 4.8 mm across its flat, standing 18 mm above the panel, flat toward the back at OFF. It is locked at OFF by a lug in a notch of the valve body until pushed 3.5 mm in, against its spring (6 N at rest, about 10 N at 3.5 mm; 4.5 mm travel); then it turns counter-clockwise (seen from above) toward HI and LO; OFF is its clockwise stop. A paint witness line runs across each stem's collar and valve body, with ticks 10 degrees either side, seen through the acrylic. Printed on the panel at each stem: a white OFF line 26-34 mm behind it and a red HI line the same distance to its left. Two identical black moulded burner knobs (for example Whirlpool WP98006102, to match the valve's stem): 44 mm across, 33 mm tall (a 14 mm skirt, a 3 mm top, a 36 x 9 x 16 mm grip fin), about 22 g, a white pointer line on the fin's back end; a 14 mm deep D bore with a 1 mm lead-in, a moulded flat from 3.5 to 7.5 mm up and a steel spring clip on the flat from 8 to 13.5 mm (pushing it on takes about 5 N). Home, the stem's tip bottoms in the bore with the skirt 4 mm above the panel. The knobs stand upright (bore down) on the panel: the left one at x 0.235, y 0.140 m with its pointer 60 degrees clockwise of OFF, the right one at x 0.235, y -0.140 m with its pointer 60 degrees counter-clockwise of OFF. Both arms start in their ready pose.
scoring: Scored every control step from the knobs' and stems' poses; the score at the end of the trial counts. 0 for the whole trial if, at any time, either valve stem turns more than 10 degrees from OFF (the gas is on), whatever happens after. Otherwise, 1.0 once both knobs are seated at OFF, no part of either gripper is within 2 cm of either knob, and nothing has moved more than 1 mm over the preceding 1 s, all held for 1 s (20 control steps in a row). Else, at the end, for each stem: 0.45 if a knob is seated on it (its bore within 1.5 mm of the stem's axis, tilted no more than 3 degrees, its skirt within 5 mm of the panel, its pointer within 5 degrees of OFF); 0.2 if a knob has found its flat but is not home (bore within 1.5 mm, tilt within 5 degrees, skirt within 12 mm of the panel, pointer within 10 degrees of OFF); otherwise 0. A knob resting unaligned on a stem's tip stands 14.5 mm up and earns nothing. One knob counts for one stem only. In a real trial: the stems' witness lines are watched on video through the acrylic front (ticks at 10 degrees), the skirt's gap with a feeler gauge or ruler, the pointer on a top photo against the printed OFF line, the 2 cm clearance by eye.
reset_notes: Pull both knobs off (straight up), check both stems are at OFF (witness marks lined up), and set each knob upright on its taped spot with its pointer at its marked start angle.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at real size. The knob's D bore, lead-in and moulded flat are convex collision shapes; its clip is a 1.5 g sprung leaf on a slide. Each stem is a D-section shaft on a D6 joint: 4.5 mm push travel against a 6 N, 1200 N/m spring, turning from its OFF stop toward LO with viscous drag for the grease; only contact between its lug and the notch locks it at OFF. Spring, clip and drag values are estimates; the plug's friction is viscous, not dry.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (step limit, 1,600 steps; knobs not touched); demo: 1.0 (full score from step 756, episode ended by success at step 775)
